topic: The Antikythera mechanism — the 2,000-year-old Greek analog computer

beats.image_prompt: cinematic photo of a corroded ancient bronze mechanical device with intricate gears, museum lighting, dark background, mysterious atmosphere, highly detailed, no people

beats.narration: In 1901, sponge divers found a corroded block of bronze off the Greek island of Antikythera.
beats.image_prompt: cinematic underwater scene, ancient shipwreck on Mediterranean seabed, sunlight rays through water, bronze artifact fragment, no people, moody atmospheric lighting

beats.narration: Inside were more than 30 hand-driven bronze gears, modeling the cycles of the Moon, Sun, and known planets.
beats.image_prompt: extreme close-up of intricate ancient bronze gear mechanism, cosmic diagram of sun moon and planets etched into metal, warm golden light, highly detailed engineering, no people

beats.narration: Nothing this mechanically complex is known from before the fourteenth century.
beats.image_prompt: dramatic split composition, ancient bronze clockwork gears contrasted with a medieval European clock tower, mysterious dark cinematic lighting, no people

beats.narration: Who built it is still unconfirmed.
